title: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow
As a developer, official client SDKs cover web, iOS, and Android with the same session and track model, so one backend serves every platform
As a developer, a server-side API lets me list sessions, mute or remove participants, and end a session without a client in the loop
As a platform engineer, media routes through a selective forwarding unit or relay that delivers only the tracks each participant subscribes to
As a platform engineer, publishers send layered or simulcast video and the service adapts the layer each subscriber receives to their bandwidth
As an AI-native user, an agent subscribes to a single track of a live broadcast without the publisher changing anything about how it publishes
As a developer, the vendor documents an end-to-end latency target or measured latency path suitable for live conversation
As a platform engineer, a stream survives a network that blocks UDP: the service documents fallback over TCP, TLS, or WebSocket and when it engages
As a platform engineer, clients connect to a nearby point of presence and the vendor documents the regions or edge network that carries media
As an AI-native user, a server-side agent joins a session as a participant that receives live audio and publishes speech back in realtime
As an AI-native user, the vendor documents an integration path from a live session to a voice-agent pipeline of speech-to-text, a model, and text-to-speech
As an AI-native user, live session audio can be streamed to a transcription or realtime model endpoint while the session is running
As a developer, I can record a session server-side and receive the files in my own storage bucket
As a developer, multi-participant recordings can be composed into a single output with documented layout options
As a developer, a live session can be egressed to RTMP or HLS so a large audience watches without joining the session
As a developer, phone callers join a session through documented SIP or PSTN dial-in and dial-out
As a platform engineer, the service documents SIP interoperability with my existing trunking or telephony provider rather than locking me to one carrier
As a developer, participants exchange low-latency arbitrary data in the session alongside audio and video, with a documented data API
As a founder, the vendor documents how many participants or viewers one session supports and what changes as a session grows
As a platform engineer, the vendor documents how the media layer scales across nodes or regions, whether managed autoscaling or self-hosted clustering
As a founder, the vendor publishes an uptime SLA and a public status page I can check during an incident
As a platform engineer, per-session quality metrics such as packet loss, jitter, and bitrate are available through a dashboard or API for debugging calls
As a founder, usage pricing is published per participant-minute or per unit of bandwidth, so I can model cost without talking to sales
As a founder, a free tier or free usage allowance covers development and early testing
